messages.subject: Re: CODEX/CODEX2 wider application
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

If the copy number is proportional to the read depth coverage and if the noise structure is low-dimensional and is shared across samples, then yes you can give CODEX/CODEX2 a try. I remember seeing studies using DNA methylation data to call CNV although I have never tried myself and am not sure how sensitive and accurate the calling would be.

Hope this helps,
Yuchao

> On Jul 13, 2018, at 10:54 AM, SOUTHGATE Ben <s157...@sms.ed.ac.uk> wrote:
>
> Dear Yuchao Jiang
>
> I was wondering if the approaches you use in CODEX/CODEX2, such as your novel CODEX normalisation and your Poisson-likelihood segmentation algorithm, could also be used for RRBS (Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing) data - where reads only cover DNA fragments between CCGG......CCGG sites? I note that you state that CODEX2 can be used for WES and targeted sequencing, as well as WGS, so I was wondering if it might have a wider application for this sort of sparser and lower coverage approach.
>
> Kind regards,
>
> Ben
